name: warehouse_dynamic
description: DNS primary research environment: an indoor warehouse inspection aisle, 10 x 6 m, with two storage racks offset on opposite sides of the route, two structural columns, a crate stack, and a powered transfer cart that crosses the aisle. The drone must thread the aisle while the cart sweeps it. Coordinates are DNS: +x forward, +y right, fixed altitude, fixed yaw.
_dimension_justification: 10 x 6 m is retained deliberately. Spencer's PPO checkpoints were fitted in planar.py on exactly LOW=[0,-3] HIGH=[10,3], and navigation.observation divides the relative goal vector by 10 while capping lidar range at 5 m. Enlarging the room to 12 x 8 m would move the goal feature and the free-space statistics outside the distribution the policies saw, so any comparison with the baseline would be confounded by the arena change rather than by the obstacle layout. A larger hall is a legitimate out-of-distribution generalisation study and must be reported as one.
_layout_justification: The racks straddle the straight start-to-goal line so that a controller flying directly at the goal cannot succeed, which is what makes the scene discriminative. An earlier layout placed them clear of the centre line by 0.30 m; the goal-direct baseline then threaded the gap and scored 3/3, so the static condition measured nothing. rack_a now occupies y in [-2.20, +0.20] at x in [3.1, 3.9] and rack_b occupies y in [-0.20, +2.20] at x in [6.1, 6.9], each overlapping y = 0 by 0.20 m. After inflating by the 0.18 m drone radius, passing rack_a requires y >= +0.38 and passing rack_b requires y <= -0.38, forcing an S-shaped route. Free widths at those two stations: 2.44 m on the main side and 0.44 m on the far side, so a narrower alternative route also exists. The cart blocks 0.91 m of the 5.64 m usable width at x = 5.1, leaving at least 2.37 m beside it. Every passage exceeds the 0.36 m drone diameter and the scene is navigable throughout.

obstacles.label: storage rack A
obstacles.purpose: Blocks the left half of the aisle and forces the first lateral deviation. Its flat 2.4 m face is also the primary calibration target for the lidar: a plane returns a predictable range profile, unlike a cylinder.

obstacles.label: storage rack B
obstacles.purpose: Mirrors rack A on the right, forcing a second deviation the other way, so a policy cannot succeed by committing to one side.

obstacles.label: structural column
obstacles.purpose: Off-route building column. Provides a fixed, precisely known square return for sector calibration and adds a wall-clearance hazard near the right boundary.

obstacles.label: structural column
obstacles.purpose: Mirror column near the left boundary, late in the route.

obstacles.label: crate stack
obstacles.purpose: Low stacked pallet load just off the final approach. Tests whether the policy keeps clearance while converging on the goal, and gives a short, wide return close to the goal pad.

obstacles.label: powered transfer cart
obstacles.purpose: The dynamic hazard. Crosses the aisle perpendicular to the drone's intended direction of travel at a constant speed, so the free space at x = 5.1 m is a function of time and the policy must solve a timing problem rather than a purely geometric one.
